      - heading "Understand Angle of Depression" [level=2]
  - text: CLASS 10 · TRIGONOMETRY APPLICATIONS
  - heading "Angle of Depression" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Relate a downward line of sight to the equal alternate angle of elevation.
  - text: 24 min INTERACTIVE VISUAL CLASS 10 geometry2d
  - navigation:
    - button "Interact"
    - button "Learn"
    - button "Example"
    - button "Formula"
    - button "Practice"
  - main:
    - heading "OBSERVATION SCENE" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Adjust the height or move the boat to see how the angles stay equal.
    - complementary:
      - text: Observer height
      - slider "Observer height": "40"
      - strong: 40.00 m
      - text: "Range: 10 – 100 m Boat position"
      - slider "Boat position": "69.28"
      - strong: 69.28 m
      - text: "Range: 5 – 200 m"
      - heading "Live Measurements" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Angle of depression (∠A) 30.0°
      - paragraph: Angle of elevation (∠B) 30.0°
      - strong:
        - img
        - text: ∠A = ∠B (alternate angles)
    - article:
      - img "Lighthouse on a cliff and a sailboat at sea"
      - img "Draggable boat in an angle of depression scene":
        - text: A X 30.0° 30.0° Horizontal eye line Horizontal ground h = 40 m d = 69.28 m
        - slider "Boat B"
        - text: B
      - text: "∠A: Angle of depression Horizontal lines (AX ∥ CB) ∠B: Angle of elevation Line of sight (AB)"
    - article:
      - heading "WHY IT WORKS" [level=2]
      - paragraph: AX (eye line) is parallel to CB (ground). With AB as a transversal, ∠A and ∠B are alternate interior angles, so they are equal.
      - text: A B AX CB
      - strong: Therefore, ∠A = ∠B
    - article:
      - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=2]
      - paragraph: A lighthouse is 40 m high. The angle of depression to a boat is 30°. Find the horizontal distance.
      - paragraph: "Given: h=40 m, ∠A=30°"
      - paragraph: tan θ = h/d tan 30° = 40/d d = 40/tan 30°
      - strong: The boat is 69.28 m from the base.
    - article:
      - heading "COMMON MISTAKE" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: COMMON MISTAKE
      - paragraph: Measuring the angle from the vertical gives the complementary angle.
      - text: 60° 30°
      - paragraph: Here 60° is from the vertical. The angle of depression is measured from the horizontal, so the correct angle is 30°.
      - strong: Always measure from the horizontal eye line.
    - article:
      - heading "YOUR CHALLENGE" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: YOUR CHALLENGE
      - paragraph: Move the boat to make the angle of depression 45°. What is the horizontal distance when the lighthouse height is 40 m?
      - button "Reset Scene"
    - article:
      - heading "Set ∠A = 45°" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Current angle = 30.0°
      - paragraph: Horizontal distance (d) 69.28 m
      - text: "Expected: 40.00 m · Difference: 29.28 m"
    - article:
      - heading "Why 40 m?" [level=3]
      - paragraph: When ∠A=45°, tan 45°=1.
      - paragraph: So, d = h/tan45° = 40/1 = 40 m.
